items.body: Bourbon has ruined romances, started fistfights, improved lies, destroyed judgement, and convinced generations of perfectly reasonable people that singing at 2:17 in the morning was an excellent idea. Los Tres Mortales understand its dramatic possibilities: their debut single, Bourbon, throws Caroline Blind and CWHK of Sunshine Blind together with Troy Payne of The Wake, three veterans of American gothic rock who could easily have made something stately and respectable. Thank God they went for the saloon instead. The lyrics leave busted bottles, motel sheets, gasoline, libation-drenched lies, and poor decisions scattered around. The song narrates the story of Blackout Bourbon Baby staggering through this chaos, laughing and smashing whatever’s left to prevent morning from revealing anything. Somewhere between downtown and oblivion, two people continue dancing because sobriety would end the argument forever. CWHK builds the track around drums that hit with blunt purpose and guitars carrying enough weight to make the floorboards complain. Payne steps into the song sounding tightly wound, severe, possibly one drink away from delivering a lecture nobody requested. Then Blind answers him. Her voice brings mischief into the argument, loosening his collar one button at a time while the two circle the fictional Blackout Bourbon Baby from opposite sides. “CWHK gave us the music and the title…and Troy came up with the story of the Blackout Bourbon Baby,” says Blind. “I knew it would be perfect to respond to his character by becoming the voice of the Bourbon Baby herself, telling him to chill out and stop being so tight-laced. The back and forth between two people trying to convince each other of their point of view creates a tension you just don’t get from a single voice. It’s also only somewhat reflective of my actual friendship with Troy!” That “somewhat” is doing magnificent work. The pleasure comes from hearing two personalities collide rather than politely alternate. Payne bears down; Blind needles him. One voice wants control, the other keeps opening another bottle. Their exchange gives Bourbon the shape of an argument that became flirtation somewhere around closing time, and will probably become an argument again before breakfast. Rich W tears through the middle with a lead guitar break that adds another streak of poor planning. Los Tres Mortales themselves began almost as casually. “Some people get together with their friends and play board games or have barbecues,” Blind quips. “When we get together, we share whatever music we’re working on, somebody jumps in with an idea, and suddenly we’re all working together. My advice? Write music with your friends. Collaborate. Celebrate. People were doing it for millennia before the internet!” There are worse manifestos. Tintin’s video wisely avoids sophistication. Blind and Payne perform in front of a wall of fire because sometimes a wall of fire is exactly what civilization has been building toward. Flames leap behind them while both singers attack their roles with the delighted seriousness of people who know melodrama becomes much more enjoyable once you stop apologizing for it. The result is funny, theatrical, cheap-looking in the complimentary midnight-movie sense, and perfectly suited to a song named after brown liquor. Watch below: Produced by CWHK and mastered by William Faith, Bourbon carries decades of experience without behaving like anybody has been appointed curator of the past. Los Tres Mortales sound pleased to be here, pleased to be loud, and especially pleased to discover that friendship, guitars, alcohol mythology, and gratuitous fire remain perfectly serviceable reasons to start a band. Listen to Bourbon below and order the single here. items._cn_summary: Los Tres Mortales 由 The Wake 的 Troy Payne、Sunshine Blind 的 Caroline Blind 与 CWHK 组成，三位美国哥特摇滚老兵在洛杉矶联手推出首支单曲《Bourbon》。歌曲以沉重鼓点与厚重吉他为骨架，构建出酒吧式的粗粝氛围。歌词围绕"Blackout Bourbon Baby"展开，描绘深夜的宿醉、谎言与混乱场景。Payne 的演唱紧绷严厉，Blind 则以戏谑的声音与其对唱，两人之间的拉扯构成歌曲核心张力，中段 Rich W 的吉他独奏进一步强化失控感。整体制作偏向传统哥特摇滚框架，融入一定叙事性与戏剧化对唱设计，但对于追求前卫实验声响的听众而言，创新幅度有限。

items.album: Noodle Therapy / The Dip (Video)
items.body:
It’s been lovely seeing Noodle Therapy’s Field Notes find a way into people’s listening habits since its release in June. It’s evidently a record people are returning to, calling a favorite of the year (!) and seemingly finding a bit of comfort in its approach.

 Previously just a 60-second teaser, we have an extended video into Noodle Therapy’s world today, with the full version of The Dip . Co-written with Dennis White (1/3rd of Quiet Places ), it’s one of the album’s more abstract and mysterious tracks, and a nice example of the curiosity and experimentation that runs throughout the album.

 The video features footage shot near Noodle Therapy’s (Dan’s) home in Brighton, with Dan taking care of the filming, editing, and direction himself.

items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. items.body:
Though this recording documents the work of thirteen of Belgium's most innovative ensembles, the real star is the Park Abbey located just outside Leuven and founded in 1129. Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. The result is a mostly instrumental collection that mines the riches of Belgian folk and world music traditions, including Romani scales,
La Pump
rhythms, and accordion-based
bal-musette
flavors.
For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑来自芬兰手风琴演奏家玛丽亚·卡拉涅米与钢琴家蒂莫·阿拉科蒂拉的合作，二人搭档长达三十五年，已形成高度默契的即兴对话。整张专辑以北欧传统民谣为核心，同时收录原创作品，还包括皮亚佐拉的《遗忘》和一首芬兰风格的探戈。卡拉涅米的手风琴以旋律见长，阿拉科蒂拉的钢琴不仅支撑框架，还增添独立表达，使每首作品都呈现出精致的质感。多数曲目保持二人编制，偶尔加入弦乐四重奏或无词人声，编曲克制内敛。整体氛围平静流畅，不追求炫技，而是以旋律本身的探索为乐趣。

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了贝宁歌手兼巫毒教实践者Antoine Dougbé与Orchestre Poly-Rythmo在1977至1982年间的合作作品。Dougbé以独特的拍腿Cavacha节奏为核心，这种节奏由鼓手Belobi Meridjo从火车行进节奏中提炼，后来风靡刚果流行乐界。乐评指出此辑与其他Poly-Rythmo合辑的差异在于古巴son影响的显著增强，尤其体现在开篇曲目中。音乐在七十年代根基上融入了八十年代的合成器音色与塑料质感的吉他，作品如《Ma Won Min Towe Leo》以合成器铺垫开场，闪亮吉他与踩镫密集律动交织，后期吉他开始分向发展。由Analog Africa这一专注非洲再版的独立小厂发行，整体呈现出浓厚的非洲本土节奏、古巴元素与刚果伦巴的跨文化交融风貌。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment
(Review)
Carolina Chocolate Drops -
Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Dominique Cravic与Les Primitifs du futur的第五张作品，由地下漫画家Robert Crumb担任封面绘制。专辑风格难以归类，融合法国bal-musette手风琴传统、拉格泰姆、jug band、法国香颂与skiffle等多种元素，器乐组合极为丰富，包括手风琴、萨克斯、木琴、单簧管、班卓琴、尤克里里、特雷门琴、夏威夷吉他、风笛及音乐锯。Cravic以近似Maurice Chevalier的念唱方式演绎27首短曲，曲目多改编自老式78转唱片，包括1925年的《Ukulele Lady》以及向已故法国抵抗运动女歌手Juliette Gréco致敬的作品。整体呈现出考古式挖掘旧时代音乐的态度，由七旬左右的音乐家以严肃投入的态度重新激活被遗忘的流派与曲调。

items._cn_summary: 普瑞姆弦乐四重奏推出「解锁你的内在作曲家」系列合作计划，作曲家大卫·祖宾斯基的《Two Views of a Prayer》是该系列的首支作品。2025年11月在费城自由图书馆首演，演出邀请了人声歌手厄休拉·拉克、打击乐手泰肖恩·索雷以及小提琴家卡洛斯·圣地亚哥共同参与编创与演奏。作品在不足四分钟内完成从粗粝到抒情的往返转换，展现出编配上的细腻处理与饱满能量。乐评将这张作品视为了解普瑞姆四重奏跨界风格的最佳入口。该合作模式让演奏者同时参与创作过程，打破了传统作曲家的单一主导地位，体现了当代室内乐在演奏实践层面的新探索。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是丹麦三人组GuldGanger的首张数字EP，由北欧民谣界资深主唱Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目大多基于传统音乐素材，成员各自带来不同视角进行重新诠释。开场曲以粗犷的小跑节奏展示了主唱极具说服力的嗓音；唯一的原创曲目由乐队成员Morten Musicus贡献，引入口弦和风笛形成强劲推动力。传统曲调中加入扬琴作为细腻背景，口弦的柔和音色为乐器增添额外层次，终曲的器乐部分混合长笛与弦乐，产生令人兴奋的失衡感。整体氛围古朴而略带粗粝，展现了乐队超出新人水平的成熟度。这张EP更像是引子而非完整宣言，五首曲目的体量也限制了其深度，但从世界音乐与跨界实验的角度来看仍有值得关注之处。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.
items.label: Taragot
items._genre: Scandinavian folk / chamber improvisation / experimental traditional
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由瑞典小提琴手与两位挪威音乐家组成三重奏，对斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲进行非常规诠释。素材多源自挪威和瑞典的民间旋律，但演奏方式远离舞曲功能，更接近室内乐式的亲密对话——三位乐手沉浸在音乐内部的深层探索中，揭示旋律之下的暗流与隐喻。专辑以挪威 Setesdal 地区的 'Fossgrimen' 开篇，呼应民间传说中瀑布精灵将小提琴技艺传授给凡人的神秘叙事。乐手各自具有跨界背景：主奏横笛/萨克斯/风笛手融合北欧与欧洲传统乐器，鼓手兼作曲家致力于模糊流派边界。编曲中传统旋律逐渐碎裂、瓦解，呈现出对民间音乐内在可能性的实验性解构。整体气质安静、内省，带有北欧民间传统特有的幽暗诗意。

items.artist: Gunfire Survivors speak from The Forgotten Parts of Chicago
items.excerpt:
Editor's note:
When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago.

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / documentary / soundscape
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑并非传统意义上的音乐作品，而是录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥枪支暴力幸存者社区进行的一次田野录音项目。二十五位受枪支暴力影响的居民——年龄从十七岁到六十七岁——在一栋老屋前廊上自发讲述个人经历，部分参与者还有即兴说唱。录制当天正值特朗普下令国民警卫队进驻芝加哥，背景音中混杂着机场航道下的日常声响、街区的流浪狗与蚊虫。项目收益捐给Cure Violence Global。从声音艺术与田野录音的角度看，这是一件具有强烈社会纪实意味的声音文献，编辑明确指出没有添加任何音乐，纯靠环境声与人的讲述构建作品。作品在艺术定位上接近实验性声音纪录片，兼具社会学田野录音与社区口述史的性质。

items.body: Skinny Puppy released their second studio album, “Mind: The Perpetual Intercourse,” through Nettwerk on 5 September 1986. The Vancouver industrial band’s sophomore record turns 40 this year. It is the album that introduced keyboardist Dwayne Goettel to the lineup and pushed the group’s sound away from its early synth-pop leanings toward a heavier, sample-driven style. Dave Ogilvie and cEvin Key produced, engineered and mixed the album, which was released on vinyl and cassette through Nettwerk in Canada and the US and through Play It Again Sam in Europe; Capitol Records-EMI handled Canadian distribution, a deal that expanded the record’s retail reach from roughly 200 to 1,700 stores across the country. The cover, a photograph by frequent collaborator Steven R. Gilmore taken from a pornographic film he saw on a hotel television in New York City, later won Best Album Art at the 1987 CASBY Awards and landed the record on one of Tipper Gore’s Parents Music Resource Center lists. A 1988 CD reissue on Capitol Records added four bonus tracks, including the single “Chainsaw,” to the original nine-song lineup. The lead single, “Dig It,” received regular MTV airplay and a Billboard recommendation, and “Stairs and Flowers” followed as a second single; Skinny Puppy toured North America and Europe with Severed Heads to support the release. “Mind: The Perpetual Intercourse” streams on Bandcamp and is also available on Spotify. Mind: The Perpetual Intercourse by Skinny Puppy About Skinny Puppy Skinny Puppy started in Vancouver, Canada, in 1982 as a side project for drummer cEvin Key (born Kevin Crompton), who was also playing in the new wave band Images in Vogue. Key brought in vocalist Nivek Ogre (Kevin Ogilvie), and the two adopted stage names to tell the two Kevins apart. The pair self-released the “Back & Forth” EP in 1983 and signed to the Vancouver label Nettwerk that same year. A second EP, “Remission,” followed in December 1984, and the debut album, “Bites,” arrived in 1985 with Bill Leeb, performing as Wilhelm Schroeder, on bass synth and backing vocals. Leeb left in 1986 to start Front Line Assembly, and Key hired keyboardist Dwayne Goettel to replace him. Goettel, a classically trained pianist with a background in samplers and the Ensoniq Mirage, had met Key the year before, when his band Water opened for Skinny Puppy. He made his first appearance on record on “Mind: The Perpetual Intercourse,” released 5 September 1986. Key later called Goettel “the master of sampling.” Skinny Puppy went on to release “Cleanse Fold and Manipulate” (1987), “VIVIsectVI” (1988), “Rabies” (1989, featuring Ministry’s Al Jourgensen), “Too Dark Park” (1990) and “Last Rights” (1992), their final album for Nettwerk. In 1993 the band signed to Rick Rubin’s American Recordings and moved to Los Angeles to record “The Process.” Ogre left the band in June 1995, and Goettel died two months later, on 23 August 1995, at the age of 31. Key and producer Dave “Rave” Ogilvie completed “The Process,” releasing it in 1996 in Goettel’s memory. Skinny Puppy reunited for a one-off show in Dresden, Germany, in 2000 and became a full-time act again in 2003 with producer Mark Walk, releasing “The Greater Wrong of the Right” (2004), “Mythmaker” (2007), “HanDover” (2011) and “Weapon” (2013). “Mind: The Perpetual Intercourse” turns 40 in 2026 as the first Skinny Puppy album to feature Goettel, who remained with the band until his death in 1995.
items._cn_summary: 本文为Skinny Puppy第二张录音室专辑《Mind: The Perpetual Intercourse》发行40周年的资讯回顾。该作于1986年由Nettwerk厂牌发行，是乐队从早期合成器流行向采样驱动工业风格转折的关键节点。新成员Dwayne Goettel的加入为乐队带来古典钢琴背景与Ensoniq Mirage采样器技术，推动了声音设计的转型。专辑封面源自摄影师Steven R. Gilmore在纽约酒店电视中截取的影像，曾获CASBY奖最佳专辑美术，并因内容争议被列入PMRC审查名单。首支单曲《Dig It》获得MTV常规播放与Billboard推荐，1988年Capitol再版追加四首曲目。整体内容以历史回顾和发行信息为主，缺乏对音乐本体深入的分析与评论。

items.body: Berlin darkwave and synthpop band Blutengel released the single and video “Afterlife” on 4 September 2026 via Out Of Line Music. The track is the third single from Blutengel’s upcoming studio album, due in early 2027, following “The Devil” in October 2025 and “Schwarzer Engel” in June 2026. “Afterlife” is a slow-building darkwave track built on melancholic, cinematic electronics carried by a steady pulse. The song combines layered synthesizer parts with a melodic hook, moving between an introspective verse structure and a club-ready tempo. The single arrives ahead of Blutengel’s headline appearance at Dark Summer Open Air Vol. 2, at Wasserschloss Klaffenbach in Chemnitz, on 12 September 2026, with Chrom, Destroy Me Again and Ghostbells confirmed as support. Out Of Line Music describes the show as nearing a sellout. About Blutengel Blutengel was formed in Berlin in 1998 by singer Chris Pohl after he left Seelenkrank, and released its debut album, “Child of Glass,” in 1999. Ulrike Goldmann joined as co-vocalist in 2005 and remains in the band alongside Pohl. Blutengel has released its albums through Out Of Line Music, building a chart record in Germany that includes “Monument” (No. 4, 2013), “Omen” (No. 4, 2015), “Leitbild” (No. 4, 2017), “Un:Gott” (No. 2, 2019) and “Erlösung – The Victory of Light” (No. 4, 2021). Its most recent studio album, “Dämonen: Sturm,” was released in February 2025. Blutengel has since issued “The Devil,” “Schwarzer Engel” and now “Afterlife” as singles ahead of a new studio album planned for early 2027.

items.body: Striped Light, the long-running collaborative project of English musician and producer Benge (Creep Show, Wrangler, John Foxx and the Maths), releases its debut album “For All This Beauty” on 6 November 2026 via MemeTune. The nine-track record of electronic pop gathers a rotating cast of vocalists and co-writers: Hannah Peel, Elizabeth Bernholz of Gazelle Twin, Serafina Steer, Tara Busch of I Speak Machine, Juliana Venter and Sam Genders of Tunng. The album launches today with its first single, “Atoms”, featuring Tara Busch. Watch the video below. Busch performs with Cabaret Voltaire (alongside Benge) on their final US tour this month. Describing the writing session behind “Atoms” and its sibling tracks, she stated: “I dream now that this record was realised when driving through the streets of LA at night, neon flashing by the peripheral of your eye, endless avenues and curtained windows […] I remember the recording session, down in Benge’s studio underneath the streets of Shoreditch.” The songs date back to 2007, when Benge began writing electronic backing tracks and brought in Genders, then of Tunng, to write lyrics over them. Genders recalled the sessions at Benge’s Shoreditch studio: “It was one of my first co-writing jobs and I was super excited to be sitting in this black box room with floor to ceiling vintage synths on every wall, Benge sitting there in a tweed jacket. I would sing melody and lyric ideas until Benge was happy with them and the songs came together really quickly.” Bernholz, who lends vocals to “Foolish,” described the track as a departure into a simpler pop mode. She commented: “This collaboration feels like a time capsule for innocence and nostalgia, made in a very different time and place, when I was trying to carve a very different sound of my own. I loved the chance to make something simple and sweet. Working with Benge’s beautiful, emotional synth arrangements, the song practically wrote itself and my vocals fell into place so naturally.” Steer, who contributed “Echoes” and “Wake Up,” pointed to the creative circle around Benge’s old studio address as the record’s lasting mark on her. She said: “I have really fond memories of making the tracks with Benge at his studio in Coronet Street, Shoreditch. The record for me represents the ‘scene’ of amazing creativity and people around that studio and Benge – something I wasn’t so aware of at the time!” Peel, who appears on “Dive Deep” and “The City,” linked the songs to a version of London that has since disappeared. She added: “It’s amazing how music can evoke such landscapes […] In an era that was less capitalised, no stag do’s or beanies, when artists ran the buildings and possibilities were endless.” The full tracklist (catalog MEME26VA09) runs “Atoms” (feat. Tara Busch), “Foolish” (feat. Elizabeth Bernholz), “Between the Trees” (feat. Tara Busch), “Dive Deep” (feat. Hannah Peel), “Echoes” (feat. Serafina Steer), “Motorcade” (feat. Tara Busch), “The City” (feat. Hannah Peel), “Wake Up” (feat. Serafina Steer) and “Sleep” (feat. Juliana Venter). Additional musicians on the record include bassist Kuma Harada, Minimoog player Max Middleton and guitarist Mike Lindsay of Tunng. The album’s artwork was created by John Foxx, with illustration by Eoin Richardson. For All This Beauty by Striped Light “For All This Beauty” is available to pre-order through Striped Light’s store ahead of its 6 November release. About Striped Light Striped Light is the collaborative pop project of Benge, the professional name of English musician and producer Benjamin David Edwards. Benge built his career from a home studio collecting vintage synthesisers and drum machines, releasing his own instrumental electronic albums from the mid-1990s and founding the label Expanding Records. His base of operations, MemeTune Studios, began life in a complex under the streets of Shoreditch, East London, before relocating to Cornwall, where he now lives and works. Striped Light grew out of Benge’s parallel love of 1970s and 1980s electronic pop. In 2007, working from his Shoreditch studio, he began writing electronic backing tracks and enlisted Sam Genders of Tunng, whom he knew through Genders’ bandmate Mike Lindsay, to write lyrics over them. Over the following years Benge auditioned and recorded versions of the songs with a rotating group of singers he had met and worked with, including Hannah Peel, Elizabeth Bernholz of Gazelle Twin, Serafina Steer, Juliana Venter and Tara Busch of I Speak Machine, several of whom also produced or co-produced their own early records at his studio. In 2011 Benge travelled to Los Angeles to record Busch’s parts in a vintage studio there. Bassist Kuma Harada, Minimoog player Max Middleton and Tunng guitarist Mike Lindsay filled out the arrangements, and John Foxx, with whom Benge would later form John Foxx and the Maths, created the album’s artwork. The Striped Light songs were largely complete by the early 2010s but were set aside as Benge worked through a run of other collaborations, among them John Foxx and the Maths, Wrangler (with Stephen Mallinder of Cabaret Voltaire and Phil Winter of Tunng) and Creep Show (Wrangler with John Grant), alongside his own solo albums and production work. In 2023, at the prompting of his manager Steve Malins, Benge revisited the old mixes and began remixing them at his newly rebuilt MemeTune Studio in Cornwall. That work has become “For All This Beauty,” out 6 November 2026 on MemeTune – a Striped Light album nearly 20 years in the making.
items._cn_summary: Striped Light 是英国音乐人兼制作人 Benge 的长期合作项目，其首张专辑《For All This Beauty》汇集了多位来自英国独立与实验音乐圈的歌手和合作者，包括 Hannah Peel、Gazelle Twin 的 Elizabeth Bernholz、Serafina Steer、I Speak Machine 的 Tara Busch 等。专辑的电子伴奏轨道可追溯至 2007 年，Benge 当时在伦敦肖尔迪奇的工作室创作合成器编曲，并邀请 Sam Genders 撰写歌词。多位合作者回忆了那段录音经历，强调 Benge 的情感化合成器编排与旧时伦敦艺术氛围对作品的影响。部分曲目如《Foolish》被描述为向更简洁的流行模式靠拢，而《Atoms》等作品则带有夜晚驾车穿行于洛杉矶街头的意象。整体而言，这张专辑更偏向带有独立色彩的合作型电子流行制作，与用户的实验前卫口味存在一定距离。

items.body: Merciful Nuns, the German gothic rock project led by Artaud Seth, announced “Nebulae”, the fourth and closing chapter of their Kvltan tetralogy, through their label Solar Lodge. Pre-orders open on September 11 at midnight through the Solar Lodge webshop, in a regular edition and a limited edition of 500 copies that adds an exclusive Nebulae T-shirt and will not be reissued. Both editions will also be sold directly at the band’s upcoming Solar Lodge Convention dates in Bochum and Erfurt. Where the tetralogy’s earlier instalments – “Kvltan“, “Oneironauts” and “Finistère” – descended into the Kvltan mythos, Artaud Seth describes “Nebulae” as moving beyond it, through “dead orbits, collapsing gods, forgotten names and the space between dream and existence.” “The complete tetralogy was conceived around six years ago, almost as an addition to the ten regular Merciful Nuns albums released up to that point,” he stated. “With Nebulae, that story has now been told in full. There are no plans for another album, and for quite some time now I have also stopped accepting new concert offers. […] In any case, we will be taking an extended break. Maybe this is the end of it altogether.” Merciful Nuns will present the tetralogy’s close at the Solar Lodge Conventions in Bochum (September 11) and Erfurt (September 12), each featuring support from Your Life On Hold and Sweet Ermengarde, and at the Bats in the Attic festival in Morecambe, UK on September 19. Merciful Nuns tour dates September 11, 2026 – Bahnhof Langendreer, Bochum, Germany (Solar Lodge Convention, w/ Your Life On Hold, Sweet Ermengarde) September 12, 2026 – From Hell, Erfurt, Germany (Solar Lodge Convention, w/ Your Life On Hold, Sweet Ermengarde) September 19, 2026 – Alhambra Theatre, Morecambe, UK (Bats in the Attic festival) About Merciful Nuns Merciful Nuns is a German gothic rock project founded by Artaud Seth in 2010, following his earlier work with The Garden of Delight and Near Earth Orbit, and joined by his wife Jawa Seth and Jacques Moch. Artaud Seth also runs the project’s label, Solar Lodge. Merciful Nuns released “Anomaly” in 2018, then in January 2022 issued “Kvltan“, the first part of a story about the origins of Kvltan and a conceptual arc around the question of whether life originated on Earth. “Oneironauts” continued that story in 2025, followed the same year by the two-disc “Finistère” on 20 November, which advanced the narrative through the exiled god Zal’tharr and the Kvltanic hymns of Mars. Side-Line spoke to Artaud Seth about the project’s direction in a 2025 interview, in which he described working outside of any scene. Merciful Nuns also released the anthology “God Aeon XIII” in June 2025, reworking 28 tracks from its catalogue outside the Kvltan storyline. With “Nebulae”, released via Solar Lodge, Artaud Seth brings the four-part Kvltan tetralogy to a close and points to an extended pause in the band’s activity.
items._cn_summary: 本文为德国哥特摇滚项目Merciful Nuns新专辑《Nebulae》的发行预告与巡演信息发布。作为四部曲Kvltan的终章，专辑由Artaud Seth构思六年，概念围绕死寂轨道、坍缩的神祇、被遗忘的名字以及梦境与存在之间的空间展开。专辑将以常规版与限量500张特别版发行，后者附赠独家T恤且不再版。乐队将在德国Bochum、Erfurt及英国Morecambe三地举办发布演出。此文实质为新闻通稿而非乐评，未涉及音乐本体分析、声响设计或创作手法的讨论，信息量较为有限。

items.body: Stockholm trio ARMOURS have released “Body (Leæther Strip Remix)”, a reworking of the title track from their debut EP “Body” by Danish EBM pioneer Claus Larsen of Leæther Strip. The digital single has been available since 24 August 2026. Body (Leæther Strip Remix) by ARMOURS Bandcamp credits the 4:20 track as “originally played and recorded by ARMOURS” and “remixed, replayed and produced by Leather Strip,” with mastering by Hans Olsson at Svenska Grammofonstudion. Larsen’s version reworks the original’s synthpop lean toward a harder EBM pulse. ARMOURS commented on the collaboration in a Zero Magazine report, stating they were “more than satisfied with the result” and describing themselves as longtime fans of the Danish artist. The original version of “Body” is included as the release’s second track. Leæther Strip is the solo project Larsen founded on 13 January 1988 in Aalborg, Denmark, and one of the acts that helped establish the EBM and electro-industrial genres through Germany’s Zoth Ommog label in the early 1990s. Side-Line has covered his work regularly in 2026, including a remix of Princess Ugly’s “The Work” and production credits on SINE’s album “Luxuria.” About ARMOURS ARMOURS is a Stockholm trio formed in late 2025 by designer Håkan Ängquist, coder Thomas Isberg and artist Bengt Rahm. Ängquist and Isberg played in bands together roughly three decades ago; Rahm initially joined to handle live visuals before becoming involved in the music itself. The band’s own description cites EBM originators Nitzer Ebb and DAF, post-punk pioneers Joy Division, and pop acts Pet Shop Boys and Bronski Beat among its reference points, alongside contemporary artists such as Cold Cave, Kite and Boy Harsher. ARMOURS debuted with the single “Confront” in May 2026, followed by the five-track EP “Body” on 18 June 2026 via Bandcamp. The EP’s tracklist runs “Body,” “Confront,” “Push,” “Power” and a cover of Swedish indie band Blithe’s “Allegiance.” Music videos accompanied both “Push” and “Confront.” A companion remix, “Push (Majestoluxe Cisplatin Remix),” was also released as a standalone single. The band recorded the EP largely on analogue equipment between a Stockholm apartment and a basement studio in Enköping. “Body (Leæther Strip Remix)” is Side-Line’s first article on ARMOURS and marks the band’s first outside remix from an established EBM artist since their debut EP.
items._cn_summary: 本文报道了斯德哥尔摩三人组ARMOURS首张EP主打曲被丹麦EBM先驱Leæther Strip（Claus Larsen）重新混音的数字单曲发行消息。原曲偏向合成器流行，Leæther Strip的版本将其推向更硬的EBM节奏方向，制作与母带处理由Hans Olsson完成于Svenska Grammofonstudion。文章同时介绍了ARMOURS乐队背景——2025年末由设计师Håkan Ängquist、程序员Thomas Isberg和艺术家Bengt Rahm组建，参考了Nitzer Ebb、DAF、Joy Division等后朋克与工业先驱，以及Cold Cave、Kite、Boy Harsher等当代暗潮艺人。EP在斯德哥尔摩公寓与恩雪平地下室录音完成，模拟设备为主。内容本质为新闻报道而非深度乐评，对混音版本的音乐细节着墨有限。

items.body: Italian dark ambient artist Abul Mogard released the live album “Quiet Pieces – Live at Norbergfestival” on 4 September 2026 through his own imprint Soft Echoes, catalog number ECH003. The album is a live recording of material from his 2025 album “Quiet Pieces,” reworked in performance. Abul Mogard, the alter ego of Italian musician Guido Zen, recorded the album on 10 July 2026 at Norbergfestival in Norberg, Sweden, an experimental festival held across a former mining area. The performance took place inside Mimerlaven, a former mining structure built in 1957 for iron ore extraction and processing that remained part of the site’s mining industry until the 1980s. The set runs as one continuous 54-minute piece, presented across five named sections: “Following a Dream,” “Constantly Slipping Away,” “Like a Bird,” “Through Whispers” and “In a Studded Procession / Along the River.” It was recorded on a Zoom H4n Pro and is presented in its entirety, mastered by Stephan Mathieu at Schwebung. The cover photo is by Abul Mogard. “Quiet Pieces – Live at Norbergfestival” is streaming on Bandcamp on a pay-what-you-want basis. The release arrives ahead of the Berlin audiovisual premiere of “Quiet Pieces,” created in collaboration with visual artist Marja de Sanctis, on 23 October 2026 at silent green’s Betonhalle as part of the “HALF LIGHT” bill, which also features Rafael Anton Irisarri and Concepción Huerta. About Abul Mogard Abul Mogard is the alter ego of Italian musician Guido Zen, working primarily with synthesisers and analogue and digital sound processing. He has performed at Berlin Atonal, Poesia en Voz Alta in Mexico City, the Centre Pompidou in Paris, Centro de Cultura Contemporánea Condeduque in Madrid, Auditorium San Fedele in Milan, Le Guess Who? in Utrecht, MUTEK in Montreal and the Southbank Centre in London. Organ Reframed commissioned him to compose a work for pipe organ, electronics and trombones, performed at Union Chapel with the London Contemporary Orchestra, and he has presented his music with the Deutsches Symphonie-Orchester Berlin in an orchestration by Sven Helbig, conducted by Daniel Bjarnason. His film work includes soundtracks for Duncan Whitley’s “Kimberlin” and “Phoenix City,” the latter commissioned by the Coventry Biennial. Side-Line previously covered Abul Mogard & Rafael Anton Irisarri’s free live album “Live at Le Guess Who?” in January 2025. Recent work includes “In uno spazio immenso” with Grand River, collaborations with Anna von Hausswolff, KMRU and CoH, his solo LP “Quiet Pieces” on Soft Echoes, and “Where Light Pauses in the Silence of the Sun,” his second collaboration with Rafael Anton Irisarri, released on Black Knoll Editions. “Quiet Pieces – Live at Norbergfestival” continues that run of live documentation ahead of the album’s Berlin audiovisual premiere in October.
items._genre: dark ambient / live recording / experimental electronic
items._cn_summary: 意大利暗氛围音乐人Abul Mogard（Guido Zen化名）于2025年9月发布现场专辑《Quiet Pieces – Live at Norbergfestival》，由其个人厂牌Soft Echoes发行。该专辑录制于2025年7月在瑞典诺伯格艺术节，演出场地为前铁矿开采设施Mimerlaven。将2024年专辑《Quiet Pieces》的素材在现场进行重新演绎，呈现为一段54分钟的连续作品，分为五个命名段落。录音采用Zoom H4n Pro设备，由Stephan Mathieu完成母带处理。Abul Mogard长期使用合成器与模拟/数字声音处理手段，曾在柏林Atonal、蓬皮杜中心、伦敦南岸中心等场所演出，并与伦敦当代乐团、德国交响乐团有过管风琴及管弦乐编配的合作经历。该作品延续其工业遗迹空间内的氛围实验路线，也可通过Bandcamp以自愿付费方式聆听。

items.body: Gary Numan released his third solo studio album, “Dance,” on 4 September 1981 through Beggars Banquet. The album turns 45 this year. It followed Numan’s “Farewell Concerts” at Wembley Arena earlier that year and reached number 3 on the UK Albums Chart, later earning a silver certification for sales over 60,000. Numan recorded “Dance” in June and July 1981 at Rock City Studios in Shepperton and produced it himself. Where his earlier records leaned on a full backing band, “Dance” took a sparser, more minimalist approach built around drum machines, percussion and layered synthesizers, drawing on the influence of Brian Eno, Kraftwerk, Lou Reed and Japan. Numan invited Japan’s bassist Mick Karn to play on the record, and Karn’s fretless bass and saxophone shaped tracks including the lead single “She’s Got Claws,” which reached number 6 on the UK singles chart. Japan guitarist Rob Dean also featured, alongside violinist Nash the Slash, Queen drummer Roger Taylor, and Numan’s regular collaborators Chris Payne, Cedric Sharpley and Paul Gardiner. The original album ran across tracks including “Slowcar to China,” “Night Talk,” “A Subway Called ‘You’,” “Cry, the Clock Said,” “She’s Got Claws,” “Crash,” “Boys Like Me,” “Stories,” “My Brother’s Time,” “You Are, You Are,” “Moral,” “Stormtrooper in Drag,” “Face to Face,” “Exhibition” and “I Sing Rain.” “Dance” streams on Spotify. About Gary Numan Gary Numan started out fronting Tubeway Army in London in the late 1970s, moving from punk-influenced guitar rock toward synthesizers after discovering a Minimoog left behind in a studio. Tubeway Army’s self-titled 1978 debut led to the 1979 album “Replicas,” whose single “Are ‘Friends’ Electric?” gave Numan his first UK number 1. He dropped the band name for his solo billing later that year with “The Pleasure Principle,” which produced the chart-topping single “Cars” and established the icy, synth-led sound that shaped early-1980s new wave and electronic pop. A biography of this formative period, “Tubeway Daze: The Untold Story Of Tubeway Army,” was published in 2016. Numan signed to Beggars Banquet Records and followed with “Telekon” in 1980, then staged his high-profile “Farewell Concerts” at Wembley Arena in April 1981 before returning to the studio for “Dance,” his most experimental release to date. Numan later commented on that shift: “if I was supposed to be a pop star doing music for the masses, it probably wasn’t the right thing to do.” He continued releasing albums through the 1980s and 1990s, including “I, Assassin” and “The Fury,” before a return to heavier, industrial-leaning territory on 1994’s “Sacrifice” influenced a new generation of electronic and metal acts. Numan’s catalog has stayed active into recent decades with “Splinter (Songs From A Broken Mind)” in 2013, and “Savage (Songs from a Broken World)” in 2017, both produced with Ade Fenton, followed by “Intruder” in 2021. “Dance” remains a pivotal turn in that catalog, marking Numan’s shift into a starker, more introspective sound 45 years after its release.
items._cn_summary: 这篇纪念性文章回顾了加里·努曼1981年发行的第三张个人专辑《Dance》的历史背景与制作细节。专辑在谢普顿的Rock City录音室完成，努曼亲自担任制作人，采用了比他早期作品更精简、更具极简主义色彩的编制，核心围绕鼓机、打击乐与层叠合成器展开，明显受到布莱恩·伊诺、发电站、卢·里德以及Japan乐队的影响。制作上邀请了Japan的贝斯手米克·卡恩和吉他手罗布·迪恩参与，无品贝斯与萨克斯的运用塑造了主打单曲《She's Got Claws》的冷峻质感。该专辑在英国专辑榜达到第三位，获得银唱片认证。整篇文章以历史信息梳理为主，缺乏对音乐语言与声音设计的深入分析。

items.body: Mexican dark elektro act C-Lekktor combines the digital EPs “Antimateria” and “C:file” on a single collector’s CD digipak, limited to 300 copies worldwide and confirmed for 30 October 2026 on Alfa Matrix. The CD is also sold in a three-way bundle with new albums from Llumen and Implant. “Antimateria” holds six new songs: “Antimateria”, “Eterna Desolación”, “Monster”, “Unbreakable”, “Never Give A Fuck” and “De La Gloria Al Infierno 2.0”, built on the bilingual harsh vocals and distorted synths Markko “The Shape” Barrientos has used across two decades of C-Lekktor releases. Antimateria EP by C-LEKKTOR ‘C:file’ rebuilds four Cenobita songs with Claus Bita on vocals The second EP, credited to C-Lekktor vs. Cenobita, reworks four songs by Mexican cyber-industrial act Cenobita: “Confessions”, “Niño Atómico”, “Estrellas” and “Fugitivo”. Barrientos has cited Cenobita’s live shows during Mexico’s 1990s industrial underground as a formative influence on C-Lekktor’s own sound, and original Cenobita frontman Claus Bita returned to rerecord his vocals specifically for these versions, turning the tribute into a joint recording between the two acts rather than a straight cover set. C:file EP by C-LEKKTOR vs. CENOBITA About C-Lekktor C-Lekktor is the Mexican dark elektro project of Markko “The Shape” Barrientos, who started releasing music under the name in 2004 with the debut album “Re-A-Gression” after several years as a DJ under the same alias. Working alongside co-member Jamie, the project built a catalogue of harsh, bilingual industrial EBM that placed it alongside Mexican genre leaders Hocico, Rabia Sorda and Amduscia, drawing comparisons to Suicide Commando, Alien Vampires, Noisuf-X and Agonoize. C-Lekktor signed to Alfa Matrix in September 2022 and marked the deal with the 2CD “New World Disorder”, ending five years without a new album and including a sixteen-track bonus disc of remixes by ESA, Centhron, Xperiment, The Psychic Force, Fabrikc, Aesthetische, Neikka RPM, Venal Flesh, Nano Infect, Circuito Cerrado, Llumen, Nevel, SynthAttack, Chamaeleon, Miseria Ultima and Third Realm. The following month the band expanded to a trio, adding DJ and producer Dimitri Berzerk, reported in C-Lekktor adds new member to line-up: DJ & producer Dimitri Berzerk. C-Lekktor marked its 20th anniversary in September 2024 with the rerecorded 2CD “2.0”, covered in C-Lekktor celebrates 20 years of dark elektro with ‘2.0’ 2CD. Barrientos also records under the side projects Circuito Cerrado and Kromak. “Antimateria + C:file” follows a run of festival and concert dates and brings together the project’s new material and its tribute to one of its formative influences on a single, strictly limited disc.
items._cn_summary: 墨西哥暗潮电子组合 C-Lekktor 将两张数字 EP 合并发行限量 CD 套装，其中 Antimateria 收录六首新作，延续其双语粗粝人声与失真合成器路线；C:file 则与墨西哥赛博工业团体 Cenobita 合作重制四首旧作，原主唱 Claus Bita 重新录制人声，使致敬变为联合作品而非单纯翻唱。全文为资讯性新闻稿，介绍了发行细节、厂牌背景、乐队历史及与同厂牌 Llumen、Implant 的捆绑销售信息，未涉及具体音乐技法的深度评论，但展现了该厂牌对墨西哥本土工业地下脉络的挖掘与传承。

items.body: Belgian EBM act Implant confirms its 15th studio album “The Kinematics Of Doubt” for 30 October 2026 on Alfa Matrix, thirty years after Len Lemeire started the project. The fourteen-track album is issued on CD and digital, and is also sold in a three-way bundle with new albums from Llumen and C-Lekktor. The Kinematics Of Doubt by IMPLANT The tracklist runs “The Observer Effect”, “Underneath The Neon Lights”, “Pills”, “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed”, “Civilization”, “Sanity”, “Framed”, “Transaction Failure”, “Are You Crying?”, “Talking In Your Sleep”, “Beyond The Code”, “No Apologies Required”, “On TV” and “Wounds”. Lemeire builds the album’s title from a term borrowed from physics, where kinematics describes movement without addressing the forces behind it; the label describes the record’s theme as doubt treated as motion rather than hesitation, running through songs about control, surveillance, obsession and identity. Lead single “Underneath The Neon Lights” carries the dancefloor pulse of the record, while “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” is built on a 3/4 rhythm, and “Pills”, “Framed” and “Sanity” work as more direct EBM cuts alongside the slower “Civilization”, “Talking In Your Sleep” and closer “Wounds”. “Underneath The Neon Lights” is already available as a single on Spotify. Double release party with Llumen on 20 November Implant and Llumen launch their respective albums together on 20 November 2026 at mOtown in Sint-Joost-ten-Node, Belgium, repeating a format the two Belgian acts previously used for a joint release show in Antwerp in October 2021; Side-Line reported the date as part of Llumen’s “Winter Eden” announcement in LLUMEN announces fourth album ‘Winter Eden’ for 30 October, led by the single ‘The Leftovers’. About Implant Implant is the electro-industrial project Len Lemeire started in Belgium in 1996; that year’s debut CD single “Fun” credits Lemeire alongside Geert Machtelinck and was pressed in a numbered edition of 1,000 copies. Built on relentless EBM sequencing, physical electronics and a recurring catchphrase, “did you have your Implant today?”, the project has carried a catalogue that spans harsh EBM, industrial dance, electro-pop and dark synth across releases including “Implantology”, “Audio Blender”, “The Productive Citizen” and the EP “Fading Away”. Implant released the free download single “The Drive” in December 2023, followed by the twelfth studio album “The Chaos Machines Part 1 – No More Flies On The Windscreen” in May 2024, a record Lemeire discussed in Implant interview: ‘Embrace chaos through the machines!’, where he described the album’s modular-synth approach and its duet with Noemi Aurora. The trilogy continued with the limited vinyl EP “The Chaos Machines Part 2 – Scratching The Surface” in September 2024 and closed with “Judging Sinners – The Chaos Machines Part 3” on 7 February 2025, a ten-track album again featuring Noemi Aurora and covered in a follow-up feature, Exclusive interview with Implant judging all those sinners. “The Kinematics Of Doubt” follows as Implant’s fifteenth studio album and, on Alfa Matrix’s account, its first release conceived outside that trilogy since 2024, arriving alongside the 20 November double release party with Llumen.
items._cn_summary: 比利时电子工业项目Implant即将发行第十五张录音室专辑，发行厂牌为独立电子厂牌Alfa Matrix。专辑概念借用力学术语，将"怀疑"视作一种运动而非犹豫，贯穿控制、监视、执念与身份等主题。十四首曲目涵盖不同节奏与情绪层次：主打单曲呈现舞池律动，部分曲目采用3/4拍节奏，多首作品以直接有力的EBM节拍构建，另一些曲目节奏较缓，收尾曲趋于沉静。专辑以CD与数字格式发行，并与Llumen、C-Lekktor新作捆绑销售，另将于比利时举办联合发行活动。整体延续项目三十年来harsh EBM、工业舞曲、电流行与暗合成器交织的路线，属于类型内常规推进的工业电子作品。

items.album: Los Angeles Post-Punk Trio Mirror of Venus Open Their Hearts in “Unlock the Door”
items.excerpt: I never felt like this before When you close your eyes, unlock the door And I know you are right When I look into your eyes Oh, what happens next? items.body: I never felt like this before When you close your eyes, unlock the door And I know you are right When I look into your eyes Oh, what happens next? It never ends Every new love asks for an act of faith: someone has to turn the key first. Opening the heart after loss means accepting that joy and grief remain neighboring possibilities, and that intimacy always carries risk. Even the sweetest declaration contains a tremor, because the person who makes the world feel newly possible may someday leave an absence behind. Los Angeles post-punk trio Mirror of Venus meet that uncertainty with an open hand on Unlock the Door, the latest single from their debut full-length album, Never Say Forever. Margot Rhodes, Joy Damert, and Heidi Weber place mutual vulnerability at the center of the song: one person has lowered their defenses and asks the other to answer in kind. “It’s cheesy, but this song is my cheesy love song,” the band says, describing it as a piece about “opening your heart to new love, and asking the other person to open to you too.” That candor suits a love-and-loss ballad that holds sadness and happiness within the same bright melody, paying a deliberately saccharine tribute to the candy-coloured ache of early Strawberry Switchblade. Unlock the Door begins with a gauzy synthesizer figure shaped like a wordless “doo-doo-doo,” soon surrounded by cool keyboard layers, a driving melodic bassline, and jangling guitar with the spacious clarity of classic 4AD. The lead vocal suggests Rose McDowall fronting a dream-pop band, its soft, clear delivery carrying the lyric’s nervous wonder. Layered backing voices answer the lead and expand each declaration, allowing a private confession to grow into a shared promise. The slight change of pace beneath “Oh, what happens next?” provides a small but perfect lift—the icing on the strawberry cake. At roughly one minute and forty seconds, a Cocteau Twins-esque guitar solo enters in pearled, ascending phrases and sends the arrangement into full euphoria. Its sweetness is deliberate, while the sadness beneath it gives every sugar-bright detail greater weight. With its melodic precision and unabashed romanticism, Unlock the Door stands among the finest dream-pop songs released this year. Mirror of Venus’ debut album, Never Say Forever, arrives November 27, 2026, via à La Carte Records. Listen to Unlock the Door below and pre-order the album here. ﻿Never Say Forever by Mirror Of Venus The roots of Mirror of Venus stretch back a decade to the close-knit music scene of San Francisco’s Mission District. After landing in Southern California, Rhodes, Damert, and Weber reconnected and began making music together in Los Angeles. Drawing inspiration from late-’70s and early-’80s UK post-punk—including The Durutti Column, Sad Lovers & Giants, and Wire—the trio balances spare musical architecture with the lush romanticism heard throughout Unlock the Door.
